title: Graveyard runbook scratchpad — midnight oncall notes
content:
Date: 2026-03-18
Shift: 00:00-08:00 (graveyard)
Owner: Harper Nguyen (notes)
Quick summary:
- 3 pages overnight: two were noisy (autoscaler jitter + flaky healthcheck), one was a legit latency spike in hosted-api-prod-us-west-2 around 01:12 UTC.
- No Sev declared, but perf blip crossed soft SLO for 3m.
- Spawned this scratchpad to capture follow-ups + runbook TODOs while still fresh.

Pages and immediate actions taken:
1) alert: "inference-serving-queue-depth-high" (01:05 UTC)
   - Triggered for pool: hosted-api-gen-1-usw2 (dedicated fallback enabled).
   - Immediate: scaled up node group (autoscaler kicked later at 01:07).
   - Command run: ./ops-tools/k8s-scale.sh hosted-api-gen-1-usw2 +2
   - Observation: scaling started, queue drained after ~4m.
   - Root guess: sudden traffic spike + a single worker pod stuck in CrashLoopPreStop delaying graceful shutdown.
   - Follow-up: add liveness probe tuning for worker to kill stuck process earlier (see TODO RB-1).

2) alert: "service-healthcheck-flapping" (00:40-01:10 UTC)
   - Affected: redis-cache-proxy (cache tier) across two AZs; flapping coincided with an infra deploy of md-optimizer (rolling) — likely transient handshake issue.
   - Mitigation: temporarily pinned redis-cache-proxy to older image on canary AZ to stabilize; escalated to infra team at 01:20 via #infra-ops.
   - Follow-up: run controlled rolling deploy in staging with new handshake retry logic (TODO RB-3).

3) alert: "hosted-api-prod latency spike (p50->p95 gap)" (01:12 UTC)
   - Symptom: p95 token-latency jumped from ~110ms to ~780ms for ~3 minutes; request success rate unchanged.
   - Triage notes: correlated with large batched request from a customer (burst of 50k tokens across 30 requests).
   - Mitigation: disabled aggressive batching on that route (route-level override) which reduced tail by ~250ms.
   - Follow-up: create a guardrail for high-token single-customer bursts (quota or backpressure) — TODO RB-2.

Runbook TODOs (RB-#) — prioritized:
- RB-1: Adjust worker liveness and preStop timeout for inference pods.
  - Rationale: prevent long graceful shutdowns that stall scaling.
  - Concrete steps: set liveness exec to check pid and grpc health, reduce preStop sleep from 45s -> 10s, add note to runbook.
  - Owner: Samir
  - Due: 2026-03-22

- RB-2: Implement per-customer token burst protection on hosted-api (route-level throttles / queuing).
  - Rationale: avoid single-tenant bursts pushing p95 up for everyone.
  - Options: token-quota windows OR small token-bucket rate limiter at gateway.
  - Owner: Harper (draft design), review with product-hosted-api.
  - Due: 2026-03-25

- RB-3: Add retry/backoff for redis-cache-proxy during md-optimizer deploys and run a staging stress test.
  - Owner: Lena
  - Due: 2026-03-24

Notes / commands to keep handy:
- Check recent autoscaler events: kubectl -n infra get hpa -o wide | grep hosted-api-gen-1-usw2
- Worker pod logs: kubectl logs -n inference worker-xyz -c runtime --since=30m | gzip -c > /tmp/worker-logs.gz
- Query traces for 01:10-01:20 UTC: tracing.search service:hosted-api span:inference - filter:route=generate -- use trace-id list in /tmp/spike-traces.txt

Observations + hypotheses:
- Most likely root cause for latency spike: customer burst + aggressive batching + one stuck worker exacerbated tail.
- Healthcheck flaps seem coincident with infra deploys; may be handshake/backoff mismatch between md-optimizer and cache-proxy.
- No evidence of underlying GPU OOMs or kernel panics from initial inspect.

Post-shift handoff notes (for morning SRE):
- Samir: I left RB-1 with a draft patch in ops-scripts (PR linked). Please sanity-check the preStop change; might affect graceful draining for long-running requests.
- Lena: will run redis staging deploy exercise at 09:00 PT and post results to the ticket.
- Product/Support: open a ticket with the customer who sent the 50k-token burst to discuss quota options; notify Solutions Eng if it's expected (linked ticket JIRA-CUST-912).

Things to capture in a short post-incident note:
- Timeline (00:40 healthcheck, 01:05 queue alert, 01:12 p95 spike, 01:20 mitigation applied).
- Mitigation actions and why they helped (scaling + route-level batching override).
- Next actions (RB-1/2/3).

Loose ideas / low-priority:
- Add a small synthetic test that simulates large-token single-tenant bursts during business hours to detect early.
- Consider exposing a per-route backpressure metric in Console to detect in-flight token backlog.

Handoff checklist:
- [ ] Create minimal timeline doc in shared drive (I will draft after morning coffee).
- [ ] Attach logs and traces to JIRA-INFR-2481 (Harper).
- [ ] Follow up with infra on preStop tuning impact (Samir).
- [ ] Confirm redis staging run results (Lena).

Questions for morning sync:
- Does product want automatic token-burst throttles or prefer customer-facing guidance first?
- Any objections to reducing preStop sleep on workers?

Misc (notes to self):
- Remember to update runbook header with quick checklist: "if p95 > 500ms and autoscaler didn't scale in <5m -> suspect stuck pods" (too many pages are vague).
- Clean up /tmp/worker-logs.gz and upload to artifacts before closing this doc.

End of scratchpad.

-- Harper
